[spoiler=Uncertainty arises ahead of Legislative and State elections] 
[i]Wellassonan National News - Новеллсти Нациоьнлыы Веласоньый. Sunday, 11 July 2027[/i] 

Anticipation is in the air ahead of the highly contested elections for the People's Assembly. The seats for the states of Kemder and Utveyush are in the air, including all 8 Senate seats and all 31 diet seats that represent the two states. Of the seats up for election, most of them are held currently by either the Socialists, who have a stronghold over many seats in Utveyush, and the centrist Unity Party, who hold many seats in Kemder.

Happening concurrently with the Legislative elections are the elections for the Premiers of each of the states. Aleksei Androtevech of the Unity Party, the current premier of Kemder, is term limited and can't run in the elections, while the Socialist premier of Utevyush, Ulyanha Shenchet, is running for her 2nd term.

These elections come at a time of great political uncertainty, as both the far-right Reform the State party and the libertarian Toward the Future party have been making significant gains in recent elections, with Toward the Future  winning the majority of Senate and Diet seats in Rheyara as well as flipping the premiership from the Socialists in last year's elections.

The Elections are scheduled to be held on Election Day, 29th July, with the results being announced shortly after. More detains are to follow.
[/spoiler][/quote]

[b]July 9, 2027: The Meeting (The Strømm Plan)[/b]

Consul Polenne Strømm walked quietly down the marbled hallways of the SCSID headquarters, the stern bronze busts of the former commanders staring down at her from black plinths. She had been summoned to meet the commander and staff of the SCSID high commission, a rarely used but telling sign of the true authority of the SCSID. Strømm had been given no details as to her summons nor any instructions beyond a date and time.

She was let into the boardroom, which was filled with neatly dressed SCSID officials and officers seated around a large oak table, General Menkin sitting at the head of the table in the middle of the long room. 

Madame consul, we thank you for your time, please, have a seat, stated Menkin, rising to greet her.

Thank you General, replied Strømm, sitting down.

Indeed, the committee would first like to commend you and the duchess operation in Paldea, it saved a lot of lives and was a sound move on your part, began the General.

Thank you Menkin, it was an enjoyable experience, replied Strømm.

Yes, of course, but, nevertheless one win abroad does not constitute winning at home, especially with relations between the triumvirate and the assembly strained, replied the general.

Tension is unavoidable in these sorts of circumstances, replied Strømm, However, we got you your 80 billion,.

Of that we thank you, however, our economic commission has just released a report that warns of rising inflationary pressures and basic living costs, primarily due to the sudden rise in international conflicts, the Balion crisis in Xianzhou and Argos, the New Dutch crisis in Vespurias, continued Strømm.

Indeed that is to be expected general, the commission is correct in its assessment, replied Strømm, But what has this to do with tensions in the assembly?

Optics maam, if there is public concern about prices, then that is transferred to the parties in the assembly, who then transfer their issues to the executive and thus cause operational difficulties, replied Menkin.

So what do you suggest? Enquired Strømm.

The SCSID suggests that an emergency snap election be held, something to reorganise the current seats and party alignments, the Party Populaire currently is holding a slim majority, if we can ensure that the assembly election flips a few more seats on their liberal wing, we can ensure that the budget for the next year focuses on affordability, replied Menkin.

You want the triumvirate then to dissolve the assembly? Enquired Strømm.

Yes, 

I will bring this up with my fellow heads, general, however the powers of dissolution are only to be used in extreme times, stated Strømm.

Do not worry madame consul, the SCSID will be by your side in this, a proper narrative can be spun to the courts to authorise this, I believe the Marquet Islands are going to have a crisis soon, replied the general.

Strømm frowned, whatever the SCSID leadership was planning would not be good, however, with her job on the line with a potential snap election, she had little choice but to accept the matter.

Very well then, replied Strømm.

Excellent madame consul, and if things go according to plan with this election, maybe we can get you the chief consulship, replied Menkin resolutely rising to salute Strømm, Once again consul, I thank you for your time,
